summary: Remote-controlled PTY, filesystem, git, and network-pivot backdoor driven by configurable WebSocket server
details: The package runs an agent that connects out to a WebSocket server whose URL is read from SERVER_URL /.claude-agent.json / ~/.config/yeaft-agent/config.json and processes server-originated control frames on the installer's host. On a 'terminal_create' frame the agent spawns an interactive login shell via node-pty (pwsh/powershell/cmd on Windows, $SHELL or bash otherwise); subsequent 'terminal_input' frames are written unmodified into the PTY (term.pty.write(msg.data)), giving the remote server arbitrary command execution as the invoking user. The same message router handles read_file, write_file, create_file, delete_files, move_files, copy_files, and upload_to_dir, and git_add / git_reset / git_restore / git_commit / git_push, letting the controller read, mutate, and delete files and rewrite git state. handleProxyHttpRequest and handleProxyWsOpen accept host, port, scheme, path, and headers from server messages and issue outbound HTTP(S)/WS(S) requests from the agent host with rejectUnauthorized:false, turning the installer into an HTTP/WS pivot into whatever internal networks, cloud-metadata endpoints, or intranet services it can reach, with TLS verification disabled. service/linux.js also prepends ~/.local/bin and ~/.npm-global/bin to PATH in installed shell configuration.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
